builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: VISE: Verifier-Independent Skill Self-Evolution with Feedback from Tool Implementations
summary: VISE replaces task-specific verifiers as the feedback source for refining agent skill files, instead comparing tool implementations (capabilities, inputs, usage conditions, output formats) against current SKILL.md instructions to propose targeted edits. The cost is an additional LLM-driven revision stage per skill evolution cycle, plus engineering to extract and parse tool source code and execution traces, which fits within a single-GPU or API budget. It can fail when tool source code is unavailable or undocumented, when implementation details diverge from actual runtime behavior, or when incorrect edit recommendations degrade previously working skills, since the reported gains are relative to no-verifier baselines on two specific benchmarks.
rationale: It removes the need for task-specific verifiers by deriving feedback from tool source code, but its gains are benchmark-relative and must be validated on the reader's own tool set and skill library before production use.

claims.statement: VISE replaces task-specific verifiers as the feedback source for refining agent skill files, instead comparing tool implementations (capabilities, inputs, usage conditions, output formats) against current SKILL.md instructions to propose targeted edits. The cost is an additional LLM-driven revision stage per skill evolution cycle, plus engineering to extract and parse tool source code and execution traces, which fits within a single-GPU or API budget. It can fail when tool source code is unavailable or undocumented, when implementation details diverge from actual runtime behavior, or when incorrect edit recommendations degrade previously working skills, since the reported gains are relative to no-verifier baselines on two specific benchmarks.

As an added revision stage over four skill-evolution methods on SkillsBench and SkillLearnBench, VISE improves overall average task success by 9.14-13.35 percentage points versus the corresponding no-verifier conditions, and raises the proportion of tasks solved in all three runs by 12.36-18.29 points.
